title: Lowering Home Caregiving Grant Eligibility Threshold to Two Activities of Daily Living in Selected Cases
what_it_is: Lowering Home Caregiving Grant Eligibility Threshold to Two Activities of Daily Living in Selected Cases

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant ADL criteria
sections.summary: Asked whether the Home Caregiving Grant will be extended to families caring for persons needing help with two, instead of three, activities of daily living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health whether the Government will consider extending the Home Caregiving Grant to families caring for persons who require assistance with two, instead of three, activities of daily living, particularly where the ability of care recipients to live independently is significantly impaired.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These include the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession and subsidised home- or centre-based care such as the enhanced Home Personal Care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) is targeted at those with higher levels of functional impairment, who require permanent assistance with at least three of the six activities of daily living (ADLs).

sections.label: Individual circumstances in assessment
sections.summary: Individual circumstances are considered when assessing persons for the wider range of care and caregiver support available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Individual circumstances are instead considered in assessing the persons for the wider range of care and caregiver support available.

sections.label: Subsidised care schemes not ADL-tied
sections.summary: Subsidised care schemes offset caregiving expenses and are not tied to the ADL threshold, with schemes continually enhanced and reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: These schemes help to offset caregiving expenses, while supporting both the care recipients' recovery and caregivers' respite needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: These subsidised care schemes are not tied to the ADL threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I have mentioned some of the schemes earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I can mention a few more just to provide some context to the Member's question, for example, the SMF, which subsidises up to 90% of devices and home healthcare items, are for eligible seniors who are assessed to require these items to support ageing in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: So, it is not tied to ADLs per se.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: There are also other schemes that there are individuals with significant short-term care needs who cannot be cared for at home or in the community, they can apply for schemes such as the Nursing Home Respite Care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: So, there are many subsidised schemes out there that we provide, and we are continually enhancing and reviewing them.
